stories.headline: South Korea triggers 'sidecar' trading halt, KOSPI slumps over 7%
stories.what_happened: The KOSPI index in South Korea plummeted, leading to a five-minute trading suspension as sell orders outnumbered buyers. Major tech players, including Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix, faced considerable losses, fueling the decline. This downturn marks the KOSPI’s longest losing trend since September 2024, sparking worries about recovery. Foreign investors also contributed to the decline by being net sellers, while Treasury bond interest rates dipped slightly amidst ongoing market instability.

With Treasury yields decreasing, the dollar slipped against key currencies like the euro and sterling. Traders are now closely monitoring the upcoming US producer price and retail sales figures to gauge future market movements.

stories.headline: Simple, noninvasive technique can assess collagen in the skin of scleroderma patients
stories.what_happened: Scleroderma (systemic sclerosis) is a rare, chronic autoimmune disease that causes the body to produce too much collagen, leading to the hardening and thickening of the skin and internal organs. For more than 50 years, physicians have relied on manually pinching the skin to assess its thickness, a subjective approach that remains central to the diagnosis of systemic sclerosis, assessment of disease extent and progression and monitoring of response to treatment.
